messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for service= inference-gateway — high 5xx rate detected (threshold breach). PD: https://p.d/p/INC-1234
pagerduty: Incident INC-1234 created by automated-monitoring — Priority: P1. Acknowledge to claim.
emma: acked (emma) — I'm oncall. Starting quick triage, pinging infra and runtime.
raj: I see a sudden 8x spike in 502/504s from us-west1 at 12:03 UTC. Error path looks like: gateway -> edge-router -> kv-proxy upstream timeouts.
lina: grabbing logs now. KV cache eviction metric jumped at 12:02, mempressure across kv-proxies. Scaling kv-proxy pool +2.
carlos: customer support sees multiple tickets: "generation timed out" across several customers, high severity. Notified CS lead.
maya: correlating traces — a lot of requests have long tail latency on backend calls to kvcache, `GET /kv/context` latency 500ms -> 2s. Miss rate spiked ~x6.
tom: the last routing config change was a partial rollout 45m ago to edge-router (route-weight). Can we cut that canary to 0 while we stabilize?
emma: good call. Cutting canary weight to 0 now.
raj: applying weight change: `curl -X POST https://ops-api/route/edge-router -d '{"canary":0}'` — returned 200. Watching metrics.
lina: kv-proxy pods scaled up and are warming. Evictions dropping. Starting to see successful handshakes to backend caches.
carlos: CS: customer impact window ~12:02–12:08 UTC, affected ~4% of requests for some tenants. Escalating to account managers for top 5 customers.
maya: quick mitigation idea: enable prefix-KV caching fallback on gateway for short TTLs to reduce backend load while kv-proxy warms. Want to toggle now?
tom: +1 to temporary fallback. If we can reduce backend pressure that's safest.
emma: enabling prefix-KV fallback for 30m. Command: `rbctl set gateway.kv_fallback=true --ttl=30s`
incident-bot: Action logged: `kv_fallback` enabled by emma (oncall).
raj: error rate trending down — 5xx rate peaked at 12:04 and now at ~40% of peak after scaling and weight cut. Latency p95 improving.
lina: kube events show old canary pods terminating, new stable pods steady. No OOMs.
carlos: CS confirms fewer fresh tickets. One large customer still had intermittent errors, but their traffic is routing successfully now.
emma: creating incident bridge and runbook link: https://meet.redwood/INC-1234 and https://wiki.redwood/incident/INC-1234 — adding logs and timeline.
emma: assigning to engineering for deeper postmortem: raj + lina + tom + maya. I'll stay on until next handoff.
pagerduty: INC-1234 acknowledged by emma. Next escalation scheduled in 30m if no update.
emma: prepping a short customer-facing blurb for status page, drafting: "We detected increased 5xx errors affecting inference requests in us-west1 between 12:02–12:08 UTC. We mitigated by scaling cache proxies, disabling canary routing, and applying a temporary gateway fallback. Error rates are returning to baseline. Investigating root cause."
raj: logs show GC churn on a subset of kv-proxy nodes just before eviction spike; pulling JVM metrics and kernel OOM logs.
maya: saving failing trace IDs and adding to regression monitor set. Will run quick replay against a local kv-proxy to reproduce.
emma: ok team — continue investigation. If stable for 20m we'll mark the pager as resolved and transition to postmortem. Oncall next: lina at 13:00 UTC for formal handoff.
incident-bot: PagerDuty note: INC-1234 updated (acknowledged).
raj: adding timeline + metrics to the incident doc. Will try to get a probable cause within next 2 hours.
carlos: CS will update affected customers with the draft blurb in 10m.
emma: thanks. Monitoring: keep an eye on us-west1 5xx rate and kv cache miss rate.
end of thread
